messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected in us-east-1 affecting Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Source: prod-api-gw. P95 latency spiked to 2.4s. Paging on-call. severity: high :rotating_light:

sarah (oncall): acknowledging, looking now. Paging infra/sre.

alex (sre): on it — checking api-gateway and alb metrics. Are we seeing backend 502/503 from auth proxy or model servers?

raj: preliminary logs show a lot of `GET /token` 502 from auth-proxy (okta-proxy) with `upstream prematurely closed connection` and `504` from alb. This started ~10m ago.

emily (infra): I see increased ELB 5xx in us-east-1 across ALB and NLB for the routing layer. No obvious host-level OOMs on the dedicated pool nodes.

ops-bot: Recent events: AWS reported degraded networking in us-east-1. (link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/XXXXX)

sarah (oncall): ok — this looks like a regional third-party/cloud problem hitting our auth proxy + edge. Short list: 1) confirm customer impact 2) mitigate routing/fallback 3) notify customers and update status.

alex (sre): Running quick health checks:
```
# curl -sv https://api.prod.redwood.example/v1/health
* Connected to api.prod...
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.prod...
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{"uptime":..., "backend_status": "degraded"}
```

raj: stack traces show the auth token fetch path failing when calling STS/Okta. Example log: `auth-proxy error: upstream error: 502 Proxy Error: connect ECONNRESET`

emily (infra): I've hit our fallback routing policy to reduce traffic to us-east-1 for new requests. Triggered rule: `region:prefer` -> fallback eu-west-1. Rolling config change now.

sarah (oncall): please confirm how the Dedicated pools in us-east-1 behave after fallback. Are they still serving existing pinned sessions?

emily (infra): Dedicated pools keep existing connections; new allocation attempts will prefer other regions. We also increased the retry budget to avoid cascading retries to auth.

maya (pm): Sales/CS, what's the customer-facing message? Severity high and multiple enterprise tenants might be impacted.

lewis (sales): I'm patching a note to top 10 accounts and opening dedicated DMs. Will need ETA.

alex (sre): Quick mitigation step: enable `auth-cache` on proxy layer to reduce token fetches. Pushing small toggle to edge config: `auth_cache_ttl: 30s` and `token_retry_backoff: 200ms`. Rolling to 3 edge AZs now.

ops-bot: deploy started: `edge-config/2026-03-15T14:42:deploy`

alex (sre): Also disabling strict health-check draining for ALB to avoid flapping healthy checks causing host churn.

raj: Observability vendor (logs-collect) is also showing delays — some ingestion is delayed which is making our dashboards lag. We're correlating with AWS networking issue.

sarah (oncall): Good. Assigning action items: alex — continue proxy cache + config roll; emily — keep region failover policy active and monitor latency; raj — dig into auth-proxy error root cause and quantify # of affected requests; maya/lewis — customer comms. I'll coordinate status page update.

alex (sre): Debug snippet from auth-proxy tracing: `trace_id=abc123: upstream conn reset on token-service: connect timeout to 10.0.5.22:443`

emily (infra): Failover worked — new traffic to eu-west-1 is normalized P95 ~120ms, but 20% of requests still touching us-east-1 due to pinned sessions and DNS TTL. We reduced TTL to 30s.

raj: tally: ~12% overall 5xx rate across hosted endpoints, but for some dedicated pools in us-east-1 the 5xx was 35% for a 20m window. Most 5xx are `502` and `504`.

maya (pm): Can we estimate customer impact count? Any high-SLA tenants throttled or timed out?

lewis (sales): Confirmed 3 enterprise customers reported degraded responses and one production job timed out. I've escalated for personal outreach.

incident-bot: NOTE: PagerDuty incident #INC-9281 created and routed to SRE on-call.

sarah (oncall): Handing over to alex for deep dive — I'm stepping out for a quick page of higher-priority customer call but reachable. alex — you're primary.

alex (sre): Copy, taking lead. I'll coordinate with AWS support if we need deeper infra-level info.

alex (sre): Running `tcpdump` on auth-proxy nodes shows SYN then RST from some upstream IPs — suspect partial network partition to token service endpoints.

emily (infra): Opening AWS support case now and asking for visibility on IGW/ENI flapping in the region. Case ID: 1234567890. Requesting updates and ETA.

raj: Meanwhile, added short-circuit to treat 5xx from auth as transient: `if auth_5xx_rate > 0.1 then fallback_to_cached` for certain low-trust routes to reduce failure surface.

alex (sre): After cache and fallback rules, observed 5xx drop from 18% -> 6% in 8 minutes for hosted endpoints. Dedicated pool pinned sessions still showing elevated errors; working on draining strategy to shift inflight sessions to other pools where permissible.

ops-bot: statuspage update draft: "We are investigating elevated errors in us-east-1 affecting API requests. We have enabled cross-region fallback and mitigations."

sarah (oncall): Good. Emily — keep monitoring EU region capacity; ensure we don't overload EU pools and trigger autoscaling if needed.

emily (infra): Autoscaler triggered +2 nodes in eu-west-1. CPU and queue depths within thresholds after addition.

alex (sre): AWS updated case: networking instability in us-east-1 affecting load balancers and NAT gateways. AWS working on mitigation. No ETA yet.

raj: I'm compiling an impact matrix: lists hosts, error rates, affected customers, and whether requests are retry-safe. Sending to CS/Sales channel for prioritization.

lewis (sales): Received the matrix — will coordinate targeted comms.

incident-bot: UPDATE: incident severity still high. Next update in 15m or on state change.

sarah (oncall): I'm back — thanks team. Any open risks?

emily (infra): Risk: if AWS region flaps longer, pinned dedicated sessions will continue to see errors; long-running jobs might fail. Mitigation: offer customers live migration of sessions or request them to restart jobs.

maya (pm): Let's prepare a post-incident follow-up: timeline, root cause (AWS networking + auth upstream failures), actions taken, and customer list.

alex (sre): Current status: Hosted P95 back to ~140ms, 5xx at ~3%. Dedicated us-east-1 pools still at ~12% 5xx but decreasing as sessions drain.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: AWS reported mitigations in us-east-1, and our error rates returned to baseline. Incident resolved by on-call at 1970123789.

sarah (oncall): Closing thread. Postmortem owners: alex, emily, raj. I'll create postmortem doc and link to this thread. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
